title: CEMTM: Contextual Embedding-based Multimodal Topic Modeling
task: Topic modelling of documents with text and multiple images
problem: Multimodal topic models use separate encoders per modality, struggle with several images per document, and capture weak cross-modal interactions.
architecture: Frozen VLM2Vec (fine-tuned LLaVA-Next-7B) encodes text tokens and image patches jointly; a learnable distributional importance network weights token contributions; encoder forward layer gives document-topic vector, decoder reconstructs the LVLM last-token document embedding (reconstruction loss); explicit word-topic and document-topic distributions retained.

datasets.name: WikiWeb2M
datasets.details: 100,833 documents, 527 tokens and 4.1 images on average; gold topic labels

key_results: WikiWeb2M: NPMI .088, LLM 2.70, Purity .435 vs Multimodal TopicGPT .080, 2.67, .414 (averaged over K = 25-100).
SPIQA: Purity .444, ARI .251, NMI .359, best among all models.
Topic-based few-shot example selection: SPIQA METEOR 31.3 vs 28.7 (embedding-based) and TQA accuracy 87.31 vs 86.09.
strengths: Handles multiple images per document without repeated encoding while keeping interpretable topic-word distributions.
Shows a downstream use of topic vectors for in-context example retrieval.

limitations.text: Relies on a 7B LVLM, needing large GPU resources; not suited to low-resource or real-time use.
Topics are not guaranteed to be disentangled; English only; importance weights not validated against humans.
